newsitem.title: USA: USDA seeks to lift bans on variety of fruits, vegetables.
newsitem.headline: USDA seeks to lift bans on variety of fruits, vegetables.

text.p: The Agriculture Department said Monday it was proposing to lift bans on imports of a variety of fruits and vegetables, ranging from dill from Guatemala to leeks from the Netherlands.

"Lifting these restrictions would provide the United States with additional varieties and sources of fruits and vegetables without the threat of introducing any injurious plant pests," said Alfred Elder, a top official at the Agriculture Department's Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service.
The Agriculture Department is slated to publish a proposed rule in the Federal Register March 25 and said comments would be due by May 27.

The department seeks to allow imports of radicchio from Ecuador, eggplant from El Salvador, basil and dill from Guatemala, above ground parts of mioga ginger from Japan, and eggplant and radicchio from Nicaragua.
The proposed rule would also allow imports of papayas from Brazil, leeks from Belgium and the Netherlands and garlic from Romania under special conditions.

It said other proposed regulatory changes include declaring all Chilean provinces free of the Mediterranean fruit fly and extending the production area in Arava, Israel, from where peppers may be grown for import to the United States.
